quote: I’m nervous, excited, scared, and overwhelmed all at once. It’s all I can think about all day. Any advice on how to prepare? Podcasts, books, anything that will give me a good foundation. I’m all ears!
cx: A first-time father days after the positive test.

quote: Thanks for the book rec! And the book and exercise ball are now in my Amazon cart 😂
cx: What he bought from the first replies.

quote: I have a long list. She says my long list overwhelms her. She has nothing at this point and seemingly no thoughts other than one name I don’t like. She wants to use a tinder like app and I went through all the names in 20 minutes.
cx: Five weeks before the due date, the couple still has no name.

quote:
I’m scared.

Not of nappies (well, sort of) or sleepless nights. I’ll work that out.

I’m scared of losing me.
cx: A father the night before the birth of a very wanted first baby.

quote:
Part of me thinks that the second I see her none of this will matter.

The other part thinks that’s probably another one of those things people say because it sounds nice.
cx: Same father, doubting the reassurance everyone gives.

quote: she's already uncomfortable in her own body. pregnancy has been rough on her her back hurts. her legs swell. i can't imagine her in economy for 6 hours. […] like 1900 is a lot of money. that's a stroller. that's a car seat that's a lot of diapers.
cx: A husband pricing business-class seats for a babymoon to Hawaii.

quote: When I started taking on clients i found forming a plan did not work. 90% of the time most parents weren't sure what to expect and just wanted to meet baby and go from there which I agreed with.
cx: A postpartum doula on the written postpartum plan her training told her to make with clients.

quote: The midwife we're assigned has never bothered to learn my name, despite me coming with my wife to almost every appointment (I've missed two).
cx: A husband's rant about NHS antenatal care on the due date.

quote: Inconsistent advice. We've received so much conflicting advice from our midwife, and the midwife we saw during the antenatal classes. How is this remotely possible? Why is there no joined up healthcare messaging.
cx: Same father on what the midwives and the antenatal class told them.

quote: Our midwife has never told us anything unless we explicitly ask. Colostrum harvesting, perennial massage? We had to ask first. Dads classes, you guessed it, had to ask. We've been kept in the dark so much.
cx: What nobody offered them unless they asked.

quote: Every single appointment we've had we've not been pre-told what we're expecting. Oh you didn't drink enough water for the scan, your bladder should be more full. Next appointment, oh why is your bladder full, it should be empty for the scan.
cx: Appointments with no warning of what to bring or do.

quote: So now we're having our induction today, on our due date. We've had no real patient care. The doctors and midwives have continuously pushed with what seems like works for them best.
cx: The morning of an induction the couple did not want.

quote: When we went to the hospitals the midwife there was amazing, calmly explained everything to us, and got a doctor down to talk us through as she was shocked no one had explained why we were even there for an induction.
cx: Update a day later, from the hospital ward.

quote:
This one goes out to everyone who keeps saying every pregnancy is different. Our second followed a very different course from the first. Our expectations and plans have been thwarted at every turn.

So this baby is here a little later than we planned. 

And the dates we planned for time off are a little skewed.
cx: A father as the second birth arrives past the planned dates.

quote: My husband got laid off, and I’m not receiving a livable check from SDI. He got a new job, but the onboarding process took forever. We used our savings as much as we could to pay bills, but ultimately, it wasn’t enough.
cx: Weeks before an induction, she and her child moved in with relatives two hours from her husband's work.

quote: I said out loud his full name and she said "yup, he has such big shoes to fill with that name, she's also been updating me on your pregnancy"....
cx: Her husband's grandmother reveals she knows the secret name and gets updates.

quote: I absolutely love the middle name, I am sorry that you guys feel the need to change it. I thought I was doing something just for him. Sorry.
cx: The grandmother's reply when told the personalised shower gift had the wrong middle name.
